vertical_findings.evidence: Two code-owned structural manifests exist and are never cross-validated. The registry owns RUNTIME_STRUCTURAL_SOURCE_PATHS (11 entries, registry_architecture_registration.py:791-803) and uses it only for filesystem path closure (`declared_paths` at :1062-1066). Conformance owns RUNTIME_STRUCTURAL_MODULE_OWNERS (11 entries, conformance_architecture_manifest.py:63-77); `_source_owner_map()` (validation.py:57-75) derives structural owners exclusively from it, and `_validate_public_surfaces` (:300-314) only asserts `set(RUNTIME_PUBLIC_SURFACE_MANIFEST) == set(RUNTIME_STRUCTURAL_MODULE_OWNERS)`. No check compares either conformance map with the registry tuple. Direct corroborating evidence: `RUNTIME_STRUCTURAL_SOURCE_PATHS` is imported at conformance_architecture_validation.py:20 and never referenced in the file body — the cross-check was evidently intended and omitted. Consequence: a new package `src/agent_runtime/<new>/__init__.py` added only to RUNTIME_STRUCTURAL_SOURCE_PATHS passes `validate_registry_architecture_registration` path closure (:1073-1076 sees it as declared) while (a) `collect_runtime_imports` never parses it, because it has no entry in `_source_owner_map()`, so its own imports are never checked against the one-way graph, and (b) its `__all__` is never compared to any frozen manifest. Secondarily, `_resolve_target_owner` (:135-149) longest-prefix-matches any unknown `agent_runtime.<new>.x` to the `agent_runtime` root entry and labels it `public_facade`, so the resulting violation is reported under the wrong owner rather than as `unclassified`. Grep confirms no test in the repository asserts any relation between the two structural lists.
vertical_findings.impact: Slice 1's declared purpose (code_design_basis.json future_capability_impact) is that later slices can move one responsibility at a time 'under deterministic import, export, source-ownership, and shrinking-debt gates'. A responsibility split is precisely the change that introduces a new package `__init__.py`, and `__init__.py` is exactly the file that carries a package's public export surface. The export freeze and the import-direction gate therefore both have a hole at the one file type a later slice is most likely to add. This defeats review question 5: the public export freeze CAN be bypassed by adding a new Runtime source, provided that source is a package initializer. It is a next-phase entry condition failure, not a current violation — the committed tree has zero such paths and all 81 Runtime .py files are correctly owned today.
vertical_findings.smallest_correct_resolution: In `_validate_public_surfaces` (or a new `_validate_structural_closure`), assert `{_structural_source_path(m) for m in RUNTIME_STRUCTURAL_MODULE_OWNERS} == set(RUNTIME_STRUCTURAL_SOURCE_PATHS)` and append an exact violation identity for each side's difference. Add one negative test in tests/test_runtime_architecture_conformance.py that writes a new package initializer into the copied tree, registers it only in RUNTIME_STRUCTURAL_SOURCE_PATHS, and asserts validate_runtime_architecture reports the missing structural owner. This uses the already-imported symbol and adds no new manifest.

vertical_findings.evidence: `_read_literal_all` (:278-297) parses only a top-level literal `__all__` assignment via `ast.literal_eval`, and `_validate_public_surfaces` (:300-314) compares that literal tuple with RUNTIME_PUBLIC_SURFACE_MANIFEST. Nothing compares the manifest with the module's actual importable top-level names. `__all__` governs only `from pkg import *`; `from agent_runtime.contracts import NewThing` resolves against the module namespace regardless. A re-export added to any structural `__init__.py` without a matching `__all__` entry therefore becomes a de-facto public symbol that passes conformance unchanged. I hand-verified src/agent_runtime/contracts/__init__.py:9-143 against its `__all__` at :145-255 — every imported name is currently listed, so this is a latent bypass, not an existing drift. The positive control test test_public_surface_addition_fails_conformance (tests/test_runtime_architecture_conformance.py:75-92) only exercises the case where `__all__` itself is edited, so it cannot reach this failure mode.
vertical_findings.impact: The basis acceptance criterion 'exact public exports' (runtime_conformance.required_tests) is enforced against a declaration rather than against the surface consumers actually import. Because the frozen downstream manifest shows the trading_platform consumer using both package-level and module-level imports, an unlisted re-export would silently widen the frozen public surface between slices and would not appear in any gate.
vertical_findings.smallest_correct_resolution: Extend `_validate_public_surfaces` to AST-collect the top-level non-underscore bound names of each structural `__init__.py` (ImportFrom/Import aliases, Assign/AnnAssign targets, FunctionDef/ClassDef names) and require that set to equal the manifest tuple's set, keeping the existing ordered `__all__` comparison. Add one negative test that appends an unlisted re-export and asserts the violation.

vertical_findings.evidence: One physical directory is classified on two different owner axes. RUNTIME_STRUCTURAL_MODULE_OWNERS maps `agent_runtime.testing` to `conformance` (manifest.py:75), which grants src/agent_runtime/testing/__init__.py the widest allowed-dependency set in the graph — foundation, registry, invocation, durability, ledger, execution, inspection, public_facade and compatibility_facade (manifest.py:23-35). Its five sibling files are simultaneously registered as target sources owned by logical responsibilities: registry_migration_validation.py -> registry, durability_backend_conformance.py / durability_temporal_conformance.py / durability_hatchet_evaluation.py / durability_native_evaluation.py -> durability, execution_module_evaluation.py -> execution (registration.py:349-355, 624-658). Because `_module_owner_map()` builds target owners from those file registrations, `agent_runtime.testing.execution_module_evaluation` resolves to owner `execution`, so a product module importing it scores as a product-to-product edge and never trips the seam. Only the new `agent_runtime/conformance/` package (registered as supporting sources at registration.py:732-786) is actually protected. Grep confirms no src/agent_runtime source imports agent_runtime.testing today, so this is a latent gap with no current violation.
vertical_findings.impact: The approved basis declares the cross_module_seam 'Product code never imports Conformance' and names `src/agent_runtime/testing/*.py` among runtime_conformance's implementation_bindings. That seam is unenforceable for agent_runtime.testing.*, and the widest permission in the dependency graph is granted to a package whose own docstring and agent_runtime_00_execution_charter.md describe it as a portable, host-facing evaluation entry shipped in the product wheel. This is a boundary/axis conflation of the kind R02 and the Skill's architecture-classification check exist to catch.
vertical_findings.smallest_correct_resolution: Pick one axis for src/agent_runtime/testing/. Smallest code change: set RUNTIME_STRUCTURAL_MODULE_OWNERS['agent_runtime.testing'] to `execution` (its __init__ re-exports only execution_module_evaluation), which narrows the permission to a correct product owner and makes any future testing/__init__ import of a non-execution responsibility a visible debt edge. Then route the residual question — whether src/agent_runtime/testing/*.py is a conformance binding at all — back to the CodeDesignBasis owner, since the basis and the code currently disagree about it.

vertical_findings.evidence: `_disposition_for` is a pure function of the imported module name: it returns `retire` for five hard-coded predecessor prefixes (:13-19) and `replace` for every other agent_runtime import (:40-43). The frozen manifest's summary reports keep 0 / replace 832 / retire 4 across 836 sites, i.e. every one of the 832 `replace` values is a machine default with the boilerplate reason 'current import is frozen until the target responsibility-owned public surface is admitted'. No site carries an owner decision, and `keep` is structurally unreachable. Separately I confirmed the freeze itself is complete and honest: 109 trading_platform files contain agent_runtime imports and all of them fall under src/ or tests/, exactly matching the declared source_roots ['src','tests'] and source_file_count 109.
vertical_findings.impact: The basis's migration_and_compatibility rule 'Remove compatibility facades only after every downstream import has keep, replace, or retire disposition' becomes satisfiable by construction, because the generator can never emit a site without a disposition. A later slice reading disposition_counts as evidence of decided closure would retire a compatibility facade on the strength of a default value. The freeze (the actual declared Slice 1 scope) is sound; the disposition field is what over-claims.
vertical_findings.smallest_correct_resolution: Add a `disposition_source` field to `_site_record` with values `derived_default` and `owner_decision`, emit `derived_default` for everything the current rule produces, and state in the facade-retirement gate that only `owner_decision` sites count. No re-freeze of the 836 sites is required.
